quests.instruction: What is the action word for quickly bending down to avoid hitting your head?
quests.question: Duck
quests.hint: Think about quickly bending your head down to walk under a low doorway.
quests.explanation: Duck means to quickly bend down to avoid something. We duck under a low doorway so we do not bump our heads!
quests.funFact: The word duck for this action might come from quickly dipping down, just like the bird!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for running suddenly for a short distance, very fast?
quests.question: Dash
quests.hint: Think about running as fast as you can for just a few quick seconds.
quests.explanation: Dash means to run suddenly for a short distance, very fast. We dash across the yard in a hurry!
quests.funFact: A dash is usually a short, super fast run, not a long one!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for running as fast as you possibly can?
quests.question: Sprint
quests.hint: Think about running with all your energy during the very last part of a race.
quests.explanation: Sprint means to run as fast as you possibly can. Runners sprint at the end of a race!
quests.funFact: Sprinting uses a huge burst of energy, so it can only be kept up for a short time!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for suddenly running away very fast, often out of surprise?
quests.question: Bolt
quests.hint: Think about a startled horse suddenly running away very fast.
quests.explanation: Bolt means to suddenly run away very fast. A startled horse might bolt across a field!
quests.funFact: Animals often bolt suddenly when they feel surprised or a little scared!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for walking in a slow, easy, unhurried way?
quests.question: Amble
quests.hint: Think about walking calmly and slowly with absolutely nowhere to rush to.
quests.explanation: Amble means to walk in a slow, easy way. We amble along the beach with nowhere to rush to!
quests.funFact: Ambling along slowly is a lovely way to enjoy a peaceful, sunny day!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for walking in a relaxed, confident, unhurried way?
quests.question: Saunter
quests.hint: Think about walking coolly and calmly, as if you have all the time in the world.
quests.explanation: Saunter means to walk in a relaxed, confident way. We saunter through the park on a lazy afternoon!
quests.funFact: Sauntering shows that someone feels calm, relaxed, and in no hurry at all!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for walking slowly and heavily, like each step takes effort?
quests.question: Plod
quests.hint: Think about walking slowly up a big hill when your legs feel very tired.
quests.explanation: Plod means to walk slowly and heavily. We plod up a big hill when our legs feel tired!
quests.funFact: Taking small breaks can help you plod up a big hill more easily!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for walking slowly without lifting your feet much off the ground?
quests.question: Shuffle
quests.hint: Think about sliding your feet slowly across the floor in fuzzy slippers.
quests.explanation: Shuffle means to walk slowly without lifting your feet much. We shuffle across the floor in cozy slippers!
quests.funFact: Shuffling your feet is a slow, sliding way of walking, often when you feel sleepy!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for walking with short steps that rock from side to side?
quests.question: Waddle
quests.hint: Think about the funny, rocking way a penguin walks on the ice.
quests.explanation: Waddle means to walk with short steps that rock side to side. Penguins waddle across the ice!
quests.funFact: Penguins waddle because their short legs are set far apart on their round bodies!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for walking with difficulty, often because of a sore leg or foot?
quests.question: Hobble
quests.hint: Think about walking carefully and slowly because your foot feels a little sore.
quests.explanation: Hobble means to walk with difficulty, often from a sore leg. We hobble carefully if our foot feels sore!
quests.funFact: Taking it slow and easy helps a sore leg or foot feel better sooner!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for walking carefully because one leg or foot hurts a little?
quests.question: Limp
quests.hint: Think about walking carefully and unevenly because you have a small pebble in your shoe.
quests.explanation: Limp means to walk carefully because one leg or foot hurts. We limp a little if we stub a toe!
quests.funFact: Resting a sore foot for a while can help you stop limping and feel better!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving slowly and quietly, close to the ground?
quests.question: Creep
quests.hint: Think about moving low and slow, careful not to make any noise at all.
quests.explanation: Creep means to move slowly and quietly, close to the ground. We creep quietly past a sleeping cat!
quests.funFact: Moving slowly and quietly like this helps you creep past without waking anyone up!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving smoothly along the ground by twisting your body side to side?
quests.question: Slither
quests.hint: Think about how a snake moves without any legs at all, twisting side to side.
quests.explanation: Slither means to move by twisting your body side to side, close to the ground. Snakes slither through the grass!
quests.funFact: Snakes slither by pushing their scales against the ground to move forward!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for sliding suddenly and sideways without control?
quests.question: Skid
quests.hint: Think about a bicycle tire sliding sideways on a wet, slippery road.
quests.explanation: Skid means to slide suddenly and sideways without control. A bike tire can skid on a wet road!
quests.funFact: Wet or icy surfaces can make wheels skid, so it is important to go slowly and carefully!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving smoothly downhill without pedaling or pushing?
quests.question: Coast
quests.hint: Think about riding a scooter down a small hill without pushing at all.
quests.explanation: Coast means to move smoothly downhill without pedaling. We coast down a small hill on our scooter!
quests.funFact: Coasting downhill lets you rest your legs while still moving forward!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for suddenly turning to one side to avoid something?
quests.question: Swerve
quests.hint: Think about a car suddenly turning sideways to avoid a puddle in the road.
quests.explanation: Swerve means to suddenly turn to one side to avoid something. A car might swerve around a puddle!
quests.funFact: Drivers swerve carefully and slowly to stay safe on the road!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for slowing down or stopping something that is moving?
quests.question: Brake
quests.hint: Think about squeezing the handles on your bike to make it stop.
quests.explanation: Brake means to slow down or stop something moving. We brake our bike by squeezing the handles!
quests.funFact: Brakes use gentle rubbing force to slow down a moving bike or car safely!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving backward instead of forward?
quests.question: Reverse
quests.hint: Think about a car backing carefully out of a driveway.
quests.explanation: Reverse means to move backward instead of forward. A car can reverse carefully out of a driveway!
quests.funFact: Drivers look carefully behind them before they reverse a car!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for stopping a vehicle and leaving it in one spot?
quests.question: Park
quests.hint: Think about a car stopping neatly between the lines in a parking lot.
quests.explanation: Park means to stop a vehicle and leave it in one spot. We park the car neatly in a parking space!
quests.funFact: Parking between the lines carefully leaves enough room for the car parked next to you!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for stepping onto a ship, plane, or bus to begin a trip?
quests.question: Board
quests.hint: Think about walking up the steps to get onto a big airplane.
quests.explanation: Board means to step onto a ship, plane, or bus. We board the plane before our big trip!
quests.funFact: People usually board a plane in a careful, organized line!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for sending something, like a rocket, up into the sky?
quests.question: Launch
quests.hint: Think about a rocket blasting off the ground into outer space.
quests.explanation: Launch means to send something up into the sky. Scientists launch a rocket into outer space!
quests.funFact: A rocket needs an enormous amount of power to launch all the way into space!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for coming down to the ground after being in the air?
quests.question: Land
quests.hint: Think about an airplane coming down gently to touch the runway.
quests.explanation: Land means to come down to the ground after flying. An airplane lands gently on the runway!
quests.funFact: Pilots practice for a long time to learn how to land a plane smoothly!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for dropping a heavy hook into the water to keep a boat from drifting?
quests.question: Anchor
quests.hint: Think about a heavy metal hook being dropped to keep a boat from floating away.
quests.explanation: Anchor means to drop a heavy hook to keep a boat in place. Sailors anchor their boat before they rest!
quests.funFact: An anchor is heavy and shaped so it can dig firmly into the ground under the water!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for bringing a boat in to rest beside a platform by the water?
quests.question: Dock
quests.hint: Think about a boat pulling in carefully to a wooden platform by the sea.
quests.explanation: Dock means to bring a boat in to rest beside a platform. Sailors dock their boat at the harbor!
quests.funFact: A dock is a safe, sturdy place where boats can rest right beside the water!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for pulling a vehicle behind another one?
quests.question: Tow
quests.hint: Think about a big truck pulling a car that will not start behind it with a strong rope.
quests.explanation: Tow means to pull a vehicle behind another one. A truck can tow a car that will not start!
quests.funFact: A tow truck uses a strong hook and cable to safely pull another vehicle!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for pulling or carrying something heavy from place to place?
quests.question: Haul
quests.hint: Think about pulling a heavy box slowly across the floor to a new room.
quests.explanation: Haul means to pull or carry something heavy. We haul a heavy box of toys to a new room!
quests.funFact: Hauling heavy things is much easier with a wagon or a cart to help!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for pulling something up high using a rope?
quests.question: Hoist
quests.hint: Think about pulling a rope to raise a flag all the way up a tall pole.
quests.explanation: Hoist means to pull something up high using a rope. We hoist a flag up a tall flagpole!
quests.funFact: Sailors hoist heavy sails using strong ropes and pulleys!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for pulling something suddenly and firmly?
quests.question: Tug
quests.hint: Think about pulling hard on a rope during a fun game with your friends.
quests.explanation: Tug means to pull something suddenly and firmly. We tug on a rope during a fun game!
quests.funFact: A popular team game where everyone tugs on a rope is called tug-of-war!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for putting things into a vehicle or container to carry them?
quests.question: Load
quests.hint: Think about putting all the suitcases carefully into the back of a car.
quests.explanation: Load means to put things into something to carry them. We load our suitcases into the car before a trip!
quests.funFact: Loading a car evenly helps keep it balanced and safe to drive!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for pulling something heavy slowly along the ground?
quests.question: Drag
quests.hint: Think about pulling a heavy sled slowly behind you through the snow.
quests.explanation: Drag means to pull something heavy slowly along the ground. We drag a sled through the snow!
quests.funFact: Dragging something over smooth snow or ice is often much easier than over rough ground!
